media.title: Steve Bannon, Ehud Barak and EFTA02240144: the calendar is a plan

analysis: The March 2018 calendar gives a sequence of appointments and a proposed dinner. Its precision makes it useful for testing a chronology; precision alone does not establish attendance.
The next-morning breakfast is a separate planned entry. The page does not collapse adjacent names into a finding that everyone met, or invent the subject of a conversation.

media.title: Stephen Hawking and EFTA00695049: the contact-details request
media.description: Stephen Hawking: the contact-details request. Read EFTA00695049 with the original GAH caption and carefully bounded source notes.
analysis: The June 2015 chain concerns obtaining and sharing contact information. The striking flight remark belongs to Lawrence Krauss; it does not become an independently authenticated passenger record by being quoted.

The original reel caption is preserved below, including a redaction description that differs from the PDF mirror reviewed for this page. GAH does not display the address. The archive landing page has no displayed OCR; the labeled released-PDF mirror supplies the reviewed text.

media.title: Jeff Bezos and EFTA00759004: what a shared email list establishes
media.description: Jeff Bezos: the shared email recipient list. Read EFTA00759004 with the original GAH caption and carefully bounded source notes.
analysis: The artifact is an email thread, with an outer Myhrvold reply and a quoted Brockman message. Its recipient list contains Bezos and Epstein among many names.

That makes the list useful evidence for a narrowly stated fact: these names appear in this correspondence. It does not establish relationships among all recipients or show that anyone received, read or endorsed its contents.

media.title: Ghislaine Maxwell: EFTA02332402 and the household-record trail
media.description: Ghislaine Maxwell: travel coordination and household records. Read EFTA02332402, EFTA00007893 with the original GAH caption and carefully bounded source notes.
analysis: The email shows Maxwell requesting a schedule change and Attaway reporting revised travel arrangements through an assistant. It supplies direct evidence of coordination, without independently establishing the actual arrival.

The binder supplies a different source family within the released records: household and contact paperwork. Its entries should be read individually. The source note does not reproduce private addresses or turn the caption’s role description into a formal job title.

media.title: Jean-Luc Brunel: EFTA01972778, MC2 and the redacted payee
media.description: Jean-Luc Brunel: MC2 correspondence and apartment repairs. Read EFTA01972778, EFTA00962798 with GAH’s original caption, receipts, denials where relevant and source limits.
analysis: Kahn’s email supplies a payment-adjustment statement and forwards MC2 correspondence. Its redactions matter: the page does not identify who receives the returned amount.

The separate apartment email concerns repairs and requests for permission. These records support a limited account of business and practical coordination; they do not themselves establish a criminal purpose or every wider claim in the original caption.

media.title: Alan Dershowitz: EFTA00352969, EFTA00338082 and planned appointments
media.description: Alan Dershowitz: appointments in the 2015 schedule. Read EFTA00352969, EFTA00338082 with GAH’s original caption, receipts, denials where relevant and source limits.
analysis: The February itinerary contains both confirmation language and a proposed schedule; the October source supplies a second calendar entry. The page preserves those administrative distinctions rather than narrating either as an observed meeting.

Dershowitz’s denial and the original reel’s 2022 dropped-suit context appear beside the association records. The 2015 schedules do not adjudicate the disputed allegation and supply no basis for inferring criminal conduct.

media.title: Bill Richardson: EFTA00014374 and the limits of the counsel-call memo
media.description: Bill Richardson: counsel memo and proposed callback. Read EFTA00014374, EFTA02662212 with GAH’s original caption, receipts, denials where relevant and source limits.
analysis: The prosecutor’s note records a discussion with counsel about an allegation and the investigation’s position at that time. Its language about possible later inquiries and an attorney proffer matters alongside the decision not to seek an interview then.

A different document records a proposed callback to Epstein. It supplies evidence of a communication channel and an intention to call; it does not independently establish a completed conversation. Richardson’s reported denial remains beside the attributed allegation.

media.title: Les Wexner and EFTA02731082: the attorney proffer and the missing instrument
media.description: Read the Wexner attorney-proffer account in EFTA02731082, pages 65–66, with the original GAH reel caption, counsel’s denial and source limits.
analysis: The released artifact is dated December 19, 2019. Its Wexner section describes a July 25 meeting with counsel; the meeting date and the memo date should not be conflated. The relevant passage is on printed pages 65–66, not the file’s opening page.

The financial-control and misappropriation account comes from Wexner’s lawyers as summarized by prosecutors. The same passage records their denial that he knew about Epstein’s abuse. The page carries both parts with the same attribution.

The memo describes a 1991 power of attorney but does not supply the executed instrument in this passage. The caption’s wider negative-search findings are preserved as attributed claims, without asserting that a fresh exhaustive search proved their absence.

media.title: Clinton CGI and Publicis: the proposed million-dollar transfer
media.description: Clinton CGI: the source audit. Original GAH reel caption, primary-source receipts and the limits of the documented record.
analysis: The reel introduces the existing five-track audit. The strongest distinction is between a transfer anticipated in correspondence and a completed payment independently matched at both banks.

The reported 2006 grant and the 2007 advocacy about CGI’s origins are different evidence types and different events. The companion preserves that separation and sends readers to the full audit for the other organizational and testimonial tracks.

media.title: Andrew and EFTA00088020: anticipated judicial review in 2020
media.description: Andrew: the separate 2020 DOJ request. Original GAH reel caption, primary-source receipts and the limits of the documented record.
analysis: The June 2020 email describes an expected legal argument about a U.S. witness-interview request and UK voluntary-cooperation guidance. It supplies a procedural paper trail, not proof that litigation was filed.

The original reel contrasts that trail with later warrant reporting. The parallel is editorial comparison, not one continuous proceeding, a prediction, obstruction finding or a conclusion about criminal liability.

media.title: Indyke and Kahn: the complaint, FAA role and St. Thomas travel email
media.description: Indyke and Kahn: roles, travel and the civil complaint. Original GAH reel caption, primary-source receipts and the limits of the documented record.
analysis: The civil complaint and the two older records perform different jobs: the complaint states the State’s allegations, the FAA paperwork records a corporate role, and the email records travel coordination. None automatically substantiates the others’ criminal significance.

The original caption and the defendants’ reported denial stay together. This page does not turn names missing from a reviewed passenger log into proof that they never traveled, or turn a conditional bequest into a completed estate payment.
